name: Optimize AudioEngine player selection lock performance

description: Baseline NSLock performance: 0.1044 µs per acquire (single-threaded). os_unfair_lock shows 1.1x improvement in benchmark.

asi.hypothesis: NSLock overhead is minimal but os_unfair_lock is the modern recommended API with lower memory footprint
asi.note: Single-threaded test shows modest improvement; actual benefit is lower memory and better contention handling

description: Replace NSLock with os_unfair_lock in AudioEngine. Lock acquisition: 0.099 µs. Modern API with lower memory footprint and better contention handling.

asi.hypothesis: os_unfair_lock is the recommended modern API with better performance characteristics than NSLock
asi.notes: Single-threaded test shows modest improvement; primary benefit is modern API adoption and lower overhead

name: Move audio profile loading off main thread

description: Baseline synchronous profile load: 0.462 ms. Small WAV files load quickly, but this blocks the calling thread and doesn't scale to larger sample packs.

asi.hypothesis: Synchronous profile loading blocks thread; async loading with completion handler would improve responsiveness
asi.note: Baseline is already fast (0.46ms) due to small WAV files, but design doesn't scale

name: Optimize audio trigger-to-output latency

description: Baseline audio latency: avg 0.43 ms, max 10.69 ms. Already well under 20ms target, but max shows occasional spikes.

asi.hypothesis: Latency spikes (max ~10ms) may be caused by random number generation for pitch variation or occasional thread scheduling

description: Remove redundant player.rate = 1.0 when pitch variation disabled. No improvement in latency (0.428 ms avg, 10.74 ms max).

asi.hypothesis: Removing unnecessary player.rate assignment would reduce latency
asi.rollback_reason: No improvement - the else branch wasn't the bottleneck
asi.next_action_hint: The 10ms max spikes are likely from thread scheduling or AVAudioEngine, not the Swift code

description: Remove isPlaying check and call play() unconditionally. No improvement in latency (0.429 ms avg, 10.72 ms max).

asi.hypothesis: Removing isPlaying property access would reduce latency
asi.rollback_reason: No improvement - isPlaying check is not the bottleneck
asi.next_action_hint: The 10ms max spikes are likely from AVAudioEngine thread scheduling or system interrupts, not Swift code

name: Cache SMAppService status to reduce IPC overhead

description: Baseline SMAppService.status read: 7.24 ms per call. Expensive IPC call to logind on every launchAtLogin read.

asi.hypothesis: SMAppService.mainApp.status involves IPC with system daemon, making it expensive
asi.impact: Called on every menu sync - noticeable delay
asi.optimization_candidate: Cache status with TTL or invalidate on app foreground

description: Cache SMAppService status with 5-second TTL. Cached reads: 0.33 µs (was 7,242 µs) - ~22,000x faster.

asi.hypothesis: Caching SMAppService.status with TTL eliminates expensive IPC calls on hot paths
benefits: Eliminates 7ms IPC delay on menu sync

name: Optimize keystroke dispatch queue for lower latency

description: Baseline main queue dispatch latency: 732 µs avg. Already quite fast for audio feedback path.

asi.hypothesis: Main queue dispatch for keystroke events adds ~732 µs latency
asi.note: AVAudioEngine requires main thread for playback, so this dispatch is necessary
potential_optimizations: Accept current latency - 732 µs is acceptable for audio feedback

name: Pre-warm all audio profiles for instant switching

description: Baseline profile switch time: 0.63 ms avg (0.40-0.95 ms range). Already fast, pre-warming could make it ~instant.

asi.hypothesis: Profile switching requires loading/converting WAV buffers which takes ~0.6ms
asi.optimization_candidate: Pre-warm all profiles at app start for ~0ms switching
asi.tradeoff: Memory usage: holding 3 profiles × 4 samples = 12 buffers vs current 4 buffers

description: Pre-warm all audio profiles for instant switching: 0.63 ms → 0 ms. ~infinite improvement (cache hit = pure dictionary lookup).

asi.hypothesis: Caching all profile buffers at startup eliminates load time on switch
tradeoffs: Memory: 12 buffers vs 4 (3x increase, still small for WAV files)
Startup time: preWarmAllProfiles() adds ~2ms at app launch

name: Measure keystroke dispatch overhead under load

description: Baseline keystroke dispatch latency: 0.04 ms avg (40 µs). Very fast - DispatchQueue.main.async is NOT a bottleneck.

asi.hypothesis: DispatchQueue.main.async adds meaningful overhead to keystroke processing
asi.note: 40 µs dispatch latency is negligible compared to audio pipeline latency (~430 µs). CONCERNS.md warning was premature optimization.

name: Optimize player node pool size for memory efficiency

description: Baseline engine startup with 8 player nodes: 27.4 ms avg (12.1-131.7 ms range).

asi.hypothesis: Reducing player node count from 8 to 4-6 could reduce startup time and memory
asi.note: 8 nodes may be more than needed for typical typing speeds; 4-6 might suffice
tradeoffs: Fewer nodes = potential audio cutoff during very fast typing (>100 WPM burst)

description: Reduce player nodes from 8 to 6: 27.36 ms → 27.16 ms (~0.7% improvement). Not significant enough to justify potential audio cutoff risk.

asi.hypothesis: Reducing player node count would significantly reduce startup time
asi.rollback_reason: Startup time is dominated by AVAudioEngine initialization, not player node creation. 8→6 nodes saves ~0.2ms which is negligible.
asi.next_action_hint: Engine startup optimization requires AVAudioEngine configuration tuning, not player node count

name: Optimize pitch randomization performance

description: Baseline pitch randomization: 0.36 µs per call. Float.random(in:) is highly optimized and NOT a bottleneck.

asi.hypothesis: Float.random(in:) might be slow enough to contribute to 10ms latency spikes
asi.note: 0.36 µs is negligible compared to audio pipeline latency (~430 µs). Random number generation is highly optimized in Swift.

name: Optimize SettingsStore singleton test isolation

description: Baseline SettingsStore test execution: 0.43 ms avg (0.40-1.29 ms range). Singleton-based isolation is NOT a performance bottleneck.

asi.hypothesis: SettingsStore singleton causes test state pollution and slow execution
asi.note: 0.43 ms per test is very fast. UserDefaults operations are lightweight. The CONCERNS.md warning about 'test state pollution' is about correctness risk, not performance.

name: Measure print() logging overhead in hot path

description: Baseline print() overhead: 0.53 µs per call. Negligible in practice - print() is only called during state changes, not keystroke hot path.

asi.hypothesis: print() statements may add measurable overhead in hot paths
asi.note: 0.53 µs is negligible. print() is only called during state changes (start/stop, profile load), not during every keystroke. CONCERNS.md recommendation to use os.Logger is about code quality and production readiness, not performance.
asi.conclusion: No performance optimization needed - print() is already fast and not in hot path

name: Measure total test suite execution time

description: Total test suite execution: 80 tests in 5.95 seconds (~75 ms per test). Well-optimized test suite.

asi.hypothesis: Test suite execution time could be optimized
asi.note: 80 tests in ~6 seconds is efficient. Most tests use lightweight components or singletons with fast UserDefaults.
key_optimizations_already_applied: Pre-warmed profiles eliminate file I/O during tests
asi.conclusion: No further optimization needed - test suite is already fast

description: Fix DiagnosticsData.== to compare all 22 fields + comprehensive tests. The partial Equatable (6/22 fields) was silently suppressing @Published emissions, causing the Debug Window to show stale data for latency, volume, mute, modifier flags, and other fields. Added 7 targeted tests covering keystroke, profile, latency, modifier, settings, and app info field groups.

asi.hypothesis: Partial Equatable in DiagnosticsData silently suppresses @Published UI updates for non-compared fields
asi.result: Confirmed bug. Fixed by comparing all 22 fields in ==.

name: Optimize @Published diagnosticsData overhead in keystroke hot path

description: Add source-level throttle (20 Hz) to diagnostics publish in keystroke hot path. Throttle guard overhead: 113 ns (negligible). Savings per skipped update: ~31 µs. At 60 keystrokes/sec, skips ~40 updates/sec saving ~1,240 µs/sec of main-thread work.

asi.hypothesis: @Published diagnosticsData fires on every keystroke, wasting Combine pipeline work since DebugWindowController throttles to 10 Hz
asi.result: Added source-level throttle at 20 Hz in setupKeyboardHandler(). On fast typing (60 keys/sec), ~90% of updateDiagnosticsData() calls are skipped.
asi.per_call_improvement: within noise (unchanged, as expected — optimization reduces call frequency, not per-call cost)
asi.mechanism: CFAbsoluteTimeGetCurrent() guard with 50ms interval before calling updateDiagnosticsData()

name: Optimize keyCodeDisplayName switch with dictionary lookup

description: Baseline keyCodeDisplayName switch: 72.6 ns per lookup. Dictionary lookup is slower (80.9 ns hits, 126.7 ns misses). Swift switch compiles to efficient integer jump table — already optimal. Overhead at 20 Hz throttle: ~1.45 µs/sec (negligible).

asi.hypothesis: Dictionary lookup might be faster than 60-case switch for sparse key codes
asi.result: Switch is faster. Swift compiles integer switches into jump tables — more efficient than dictionary hashing + optional unwrapping.
asi.verdict: Current implementation is optimal. No change needed.
asi.note: At 20 Hz throttle rate, total overhead is ~1.45 µs/sec — completely negligible

name: Measure AVAudioConverter overhead in buffer loading

description: Measured AVAudioConverter overhead: 10.1 µs per sample (47% of load+convert). WAVs are mono 44.1kHz, engine wants stereo 44.1kHz deinterleaved — conversion unavoidable. Pre-warming already eliminates this from hot path (0ms switch). Pre-encoding WAVs to stereo would save ~120 µs total — not worth format fragility.

asi.hypothesis: AVAudioConverter overhead during buffer loading could be eliminated by pre-encoding WAVs to engine format
asi.result: Conversion is 10.1 µs per sample (47% of load+convert). Pre-encoding would save ~120 µs total per pre-warm but adds build complexity and risks format mismatch across hardware (sample rate, interleaving varies). Pre-warming already eliminates this from the hot path — 0ms profile switches after initial load.
asi.verdict: Not worth optimizing — pre-warming is the correct solution

name: Eliminate force-unwraps for production crash safety

description: Eliminated all 5 force-unwraps for production crash safety. MenuBarManager: replaced 4 implicitly-unwrapped menu item references with local let variables. KeyboardMonitor: URL(string:) force-unwrap replaced with guard let. All 91 tests pass. Remaining 8 '!' are boolean negation (safe).

asi.hypothesis: Force-unwraps in production code are crash risks that should be eliminated
technique: Menu items: local let variables instead of IUO + force-unwrap
URL: guard let with early return + log message

name: Add CGEventTap restart on system wake for production resilience

description: Add CGEventTap restart on system wake. Extracted createEventTap()/tearDownEventTap() for reuse. Registers NSWorkspace.didWakeNotification observer — tears down invalid tap and re-creates on wake. Without this, the app silently stops after sleep. Added 4 resilience tests (100 total).

asi.hypothesis: CGEventTaps are torn down during system sleep; without a wake observer the app silently stops working
asi.baseline: No sleep/wake handling — app stops after sleep
asi.result: Added NSWorkspace.didWakeNotification observer that tears down and re-creates the event tap on wake
refactoring: Extracted createEventTap() for reuse on wake
Extracted tearDownEventTap() shared by stop() and wake handler
asi.priority: Blocker — last remaining high-priority reviewer finding

name: Replace print() with os.Logger structured logging

description: Replaced all 29 print() statements with os.Logger structured logging. Created Logging.swift with 5 category-specific loggers (audioEngine, keyboardMonitor, appDelegate, settingsStore, menuBarManager). All logs use subsystem "com.keypulse.app" — filterable in Console.app. All 100 tests pass.

asi.hypothesis: print() statements lack log levels, subsystem filtering, and structured format — impossible to triage from Console.app
asi.approach: os.Logger with subsystem 'com.keypulse.app' and 5 categories: AudioEngine, KeyboardMonitor, AppDelegate, SettingsStore, MenuBarManager

log_levels_used.debug: State changes (profile, volume, mute, pitch variation, enabled, debug window)
log_levels_used.info: Lifecycle events (start, stop, wake, init, settings save)
log_levels_used.error: Failures (audio conversion, tap creation, profile load, SMAppService registration)

asi.note: All 3 high-priority reviewer findings now resolved: force-unwraps, CGEventTap resilience, structured logging

name: Add MenuBarManager tests for zero-coverage user-facing class

description: Added 20 MenuBarManager tests (was zero coverage) + SoundAssets missing-file logging. Tests cover: initialization, state sync for all 5 toggles, all 8 callbacks, icon creation, refresh safety, rapid state changes. SoundAssets now logs .warning for each missing WAV instead of silent compactMap drop. 120 tests pass.

asi.hypothesis: MenuBarManager has zero test coverage for a 260-line user-facing class. SoundAssets silently drops missing files via compactMap.
tests_added: State sync: enabled, mute, profile, pitch, volume (5)
Edge cases: pre-refresh, rapid state changes (2)
asi.soundassets_fix: Replaced compactMap with explicit loop + Logger.soundAssets.warning for each missing file

name: Propagate profile load errors to UI instead of silent try? swallowing

description: Eliminated all try? from production code. DebugWindowController: replaced 2 try? with do-catch that routes errors to controller.onError. MenuBarManager: on failure, reverts checkmarks to match actual engine state + propagates to onError. AudioEngine: replaced try? AVAudioFile with do-catch that logs the underlying system error before returning nil. Zero silent error swallowing remains.

asi.hypothesis: try? silently swallows profile load and file I/O errors — user gets no feedback when operations fail
fixes: MenuBarManager: added checkmark revert on failure + controller.onError propagation
AudioEngine: try? AVAudioFile → do-catch + Logger.audioEngine.error with underlying system error
asi.priority: Last medium-priority reviewer finding — all medium items now resolved
asi.note: Only 2 low-priority items remain (Carbon deprecation, Settings schema versioning)

name: Fix SettingsStore singleton test isolation with injectable UserDefaults

description: Made SettingsStore UserDefaults injectable for test isolation. Added init(defaults:) with .standard default. Added 3 isolation tests proving non-interference between suites, round-trip persistence, and suite-scoped reset. Existing tests use .shared (serial execution safe). 123 tests pass.

asi.hypothesis: SettingsStore.shared singleton backed by UserDefaults.standard causes test isolation races with parallel execution
asi.solution: Added init(defaults: UserDefaults = .standard) for dependency injection. Existing shared singleton unchanged for production. Tests can now create isolated stores with UserDefaults(suiteName:) for parallel-safe execution.

name: Add AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange observer for audio route resilience

description: Added AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange observer for audio route resilience. On headphones/Bluetooth/sample-rate changes: stops engine, clears caches, restarts, reloads current profile with re-converted buffers. Observer removed on stop(). Added 5 resilience tests. 128 tests pass. Last correctness issue from review resolved.

asi.hypothesis: Pre-converted audio buffers become incompatible when the engine format changes (audio route, sample rate)
asi.result: Added AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange observer. On notification: saves current profile, stops engine, clears buffer caches and profile cache, restarts engine, reloads current profile with re-converted buffers.
asi.handling: Stop engine → clear all caches → restart engine → reload profile (re-convert to new format)
asi.cleanup: Observer removed in stop() via stored token. Observer guard prevents double-registration.

name: Add assertions to zero-assertion performance tests

description: Added assertions to all 13 zero-assertion performance tests. Each test now has >=1 regression-guard assertion with generous thresholds (10-50x baseline) to catch catastrophic slowdowns without flaking. Also fixed LockPerformanceTest bug: was creating new lock per iteration instead of measuring shared lock. All 128 tests pass.

asi.hypothesis: 13 performance test files have zero assertions — they always pass and provide no regression protection
asi.threshold_strategy: Generous thresholds (10-50x baseline) to catch catastrophes without CI flakes
asi.lock_test_bug_fixed: LockPerformanceTest was creating new lock per iteration — fixed to measure shared lock like AudioEngine does

name: Refactor DebugWindowController to use @ObservedObject instead of view recreation

description: Refactored DebugWindowController to use @ObservedObject instead of manual view recreation. Removed Combine subscription (setupSubscriptions), cancelled updateView(with:) dance, 6 closure recreations per update, and copyDiagnosticsToClipboard(). DebugView now binds directly to KeyPulseController via @ObservedObject — SwiftUI handles diffing. 128 tests pass.

asi.hypothesis: Recreating entire DebugView with 6 new closures on every update fights SwiftUI's reactivity system and wastes memory
asi.before: Combine subscription → throttle → recreate DebugView + 6 closures → hostingController.rootView = new View
asi.after: @ObservedObject controller → SwiftUI reads controller.diagnosticsData directly → automatic diffing
kept: Controller accessed directly in view for testPlay/testAllProfiles/resetStats

name: Remove deprecated Carbon import from KeyboardMonitor

description: Removed deprecated `import Carbon` from KeyboardMonitor.swift and KeyPulseAppDelegate.swift. No Carbon symbols were actually used — key codes are just UInt16 values from CoreGraphics. Updated comments to remove Carbon references. All 128 tests pass.

asi.hypothesis: import Carbon is deprecated in modern macOS/Swift — the key codes are just UInt16 values from CoreGraphics
asi.verification: No Carbon symbols referenced anywhere in codebase — key codes are plain integers from CGEvent.getIntegerValueField(.keyboardEventKeycode)

name: Add Settings schema versioning for future migration safety

description: Added Settings schema versioning with migrateIfNeeded() infrastructure. Fresh installs stamp version 1. Future migrations add blocks keyed by version. Won't downgrade if app is rolled back. Added 2 tests: version stamped on init, won't downgrade from future version. Last deferred item resolved. 130 tests pass.

asi.hypothesis: Settings format will change over time; without versioning, old settings break silently on upgrade
asi.solution: Added keypulse_schemaVersion key to UserDefaults. migrateIfNeeded() runs on init: stamps v1 on fresh install, runs migration blocks for older versions, won't downgrade on rollback. Migration workflow: increment currentSchemaVersion, add migration block in migrateIfNeeded().
asi.future_workflow: Increment currentSchemaVersion and add if storedVersion < N { migrate() } block

description: Re-populate pre-warm cache after audio route change. Before: after headphones/Bluetooth change, profile switching silently degraded from instant to on-demand load. Now: after restarting engine and reloading current profile, re-pre-warms all profiles to restore instant switching. 130 tests pass.

asi.hypothesis: After audio route change, pre-warm cache was cleared but never re-populated — profile switching silently degraded to on-demand load
asi.fix: Added try? preWarmAllProfiles() after engine restart + profile reload in configuration observer
asi.impact: Restores instant profile switching after audio route changes (headphones, Bluetooth, sample rate)
asi.fallback: Uses try? so if pre-warming fails, falls back to on-demand loading without crashing

name: Remove unnecessary os_unfair_lock from single-threaded play() hot path

description: Removed unnecessary os_unfair_lock from play() hot path. All callers arrive via DispatchQueue.main.async — no concurrent access possible. Removed import os.lock, playerLock property, lock/unlock calls. Simplifies hot path and removes misleading thread-safety surface. 130 tests pass.

asi.hypothesis: os_unfair_lock in play() is unnecessary — all callers of play() arrive via DispatchQueue.main.async from the keyboard handler. The lock creates false confidence because isMuted, isPitchRandomizationEnabled, buffers, volume, and latencyMeasurements in the same method have no synchronization.
asi.call_chain: CGEventTap callback → DispatchQueue.main.async → onKeyDown → playRandomSample → play()
asi.verdict: Single-threaded access guaranteed — lock was dead weight

description: Replaced last try? with do-catch in audio route change handler. Pre-warm failure now logs .error instead of silently swallowing. Zero try? remain in production code. Zero print() remain. Zero force-unwraps remain. Zero build warnings. Zero TODOs. 130 tests pass.

asi.note: Codebase is production-clean: zero silent error swallowing, zero untagged logging, zero crash-prone force-unwraps, zero TODO debt, 130 passing tests

description: Removed dead code: unused diagnosticsUpdateCancellable property and stale Combine comments from KeyPulseController. The throttle uses CFAbsoluteTimeGetCurrent (no Combine dependency). @ObservedObject in DebugView handles consumption directly.

Removed Carbon framework from linker settings. Previously removed import Carbon from sources — the linker flag was dead weight. Key codes come from CGEvent (CoreGraphics), not Carbon. All 135 tests pass, build clean.

asi.removed: Carbon framework from linkerSettings in Package.swift
asi.reason: No Carbon APIs used — key codes are UInt16 from CGEvent.getIntegerValueField(), not Carbon constants. import Carbon already removed from all source files.
